tagline: Tonga's capital island, with ancient royal tombs, a stone trilithon and blowholes
Nukuʻalofa, royal tombs and a rugged south coast on Tonga's main island
Home to Tonga's capital, its old royal seat at Muʻa and a coast of blowholes
description: Tongatapu is Tonga's main island, a flat coral-limestone island of about 260 km2 that holds the capital Nukuʻalofa and roughly 70% of the country's people. Nukuʻalofa is home to the royal family of the South Pacific's only monarchy, and Tonga was never colonised. Inland, the Haʻamonga ʻa Maui trilithon dates from around 1200 AD, and Muʻa, the seat of the Tuʻi Tonga kings, keeps its terraced langi tombs. The south coast has blowholes and a natural land bridge, and ferries run to island resorts for a day of snorkelling.

The main island of Tonga, Tongatapu is a low coral-limestone island of about 260 km2 with the capital, Nukuʻalofa, on its north shore. Visitors come for the ancient royal sites: the Haʻamonga ʻa Maui trilithon, built around 1200 AD, and the langi tombs of the Tuʻi Tonga kings at Muʻa. The rugged south coast adds the Mapuʻa ʻa Vaea blowholes and the Hufangalupe land bridge. Feast and dance shows, a daily market and Sunday church singing show Tongan culture.

goodToKnow.title: Sunday is a rest day
goodToKnow.detail: Almost all shops and services close on Sunday and loud activity is discouraged. Arrange Sunday meals with your hotel.

goodToKnow.title: Driving permit needed
goodToKnow.detail: Bring your home licence and get a Tongan visitor's permit from Nukuʻalofa Police HQ or a rental agency. Drive on the left, mostly at 50 km/h.

goodToKnow.title: Carry cash
goodToKnow.detail: Banks and ATMs are mostly in Nukuʻalofa, and cards work only at major tourist spots. The currency is the paʻanga.

goodToKnow.title: Sunday is a rest day
goodToKnow.detail: Almost all shops and services close on Sunday, so book Sunday food with your hotel, especially if you arrive on Saturday.

goodToKnow.title: Buses run on roadside signals
goodToKnow.detail: Buses leave from the Nukuʻalofa seafront with no posted timetable and are unreliable after about 15:30. Flag them down.

goodToKnow.title: Dress modestly
goodToKnow.detail: Cover up away from the resort beaches. Visitors have been arrested for walking around topless.

bestTimeBlurb: Cool, dry {months} is less humid for sightseeing, and humpbacks are offshore from July.
The cool, dry season from {months} suits sightseeing, with humpback whales offshore from July.

tagline: Sheltered islands for swimming with humpback whales, sailing and snorkelling
More than 50 islands of calm anchorages, coral gardens and humpback calves
A sailing archipelago where humpback whales come to give birth
description: Vavaʻu is a group of more than 50 raised-limestone and coral islands about 250 km north of Tongatapu, with the harbour town of Neiafu on ʻUtu Vavaʻu. Islands and reefs along the eastern edge shelter the waters, and humpback whales come here to give birth. Over 500 yachts visit each winter sailing season, drawn by hidden coves, sheltered anchorages and coral gardens. The group is also a major producer of high-quality vanilla.

Vavaʻu is an archipelago of more than 50 islands about 250 km north of Tongatapu, centred on the port town of Neiafu. Its sheltered waters make it one of the few places where visitors can still swim with humpback whales and their calves. Sailors anchor in coves and beside beaches, while snorkellers and divers find coral gardens, Swallows Cave and Mariner's Cave. On land, Mt Talau has a short trail with harbour views.

Swim with humpback mothers and calves
Island-hop by yacht or day tour

goodToKnow.title: Book licensed whale operators
goodToKnow.detail: Use only licensed operators. July to October is busiest, so book tours and rooms well ahead.

goodToKnow.title: Getting to Vavaʻu
goodToKnow.detail: International flights land at Tongatapu. Lulutai Airlines flies on to Vavaʻu, and a ferry also runs.

goodToKnow.title: Sunday and cash
goodToKnow.detail: Shops and most services close on Sunday. Dress modestly and carry cash, especially on outer islands.

goodToKnow.title: Whale-swim operators
goodToKnow.detail: Only licensed operators may run whale swims. Book activities and accommodation early for July to October.

goodToKnow.title: Flights from Tongatapu
goodToKnow.detail: Lulutai Airlines is the only domestic airline and flies Tongatapu to Vavaʻu. Check ferry times separately.

goodToKnow.title: Carry cash on outer islands
goodToKnow.detail: Cards are not widely taken, and almost everything shuts on Sunday.

bestTimeBlurb: Humpback mothers and calves are in the water {months}, when the yacht season is also in full swing.
Swim with humpbacks in {months}, in the cooler trade-wind season that also suits sailing.

tagline: Tonga's hiking island of cliffs, caves and rainforest, seven minutes by air
Cliffs, caves and rainforest trails on Tonga's oldest island, south of Tongatapu
A hilly rainforest island for hikers, just southeast of Tongatapu
description: ʻEua is a hilly, non-volcanic island of 87 km2 just southeast of Tongatapu, and Tonga's oldest island geologically. Its cliffs, caves, sinkholes and rainforest make it the country's hiking island. ʻEua National Park, Tonga's only forest national park, is known for the Big Ovava Tree, said to be over 800 years old. The seven-minute flight from Tongatapu is one of the world's shortest commercial flights.

Southeast of Tongatapu, ʻEua rises to 312 m and has cliffs, caves, chasms and rainforest, with marked trails through ʻEua National Park. Lookouts such as Lakufaʻanga Cliff and rock features like the Liʻangahuo ʻa Maui stone bridge sit along the coast. Birdwatchers look for the rare red shining parrot. Low light pollution gives clear night skies.
whyVisit: Hike rainforest trails and sea cliffs
Explore caves and natural stone bridges
Hike through Tonga's forest national park
Spot the rare red shining parrot

goodToKnow.title: Reaching ʻEua
goodToKnow.detail: Lulutai flies from Tongatapu in about seven minutes, or take the 2.5 to 3 hour ferry from Nukuʻalofa. Check the schedule.

goodToKnow.title: Getting around
goodToKnow.detail: Rent a car, take a taxi or use local buses. Carry cash, and note that most businesses close on Sunday.

goodToKnow.title: Flight or ferry
goodToKnow.detail: The short Lulutai flight from Tongatapu takes about seven minutes. The ferry from Nukuʻalofa takes 2.5 to 3 hours.

goodToKnow.title: Stay on marked trails
goodToKnow.detail: Trails run past cliffs and sinkholes, so keep to well-marked paths. Carry cash, as most businesses close on Sunday.

bestTimeBlurb: Hike in the cool, dry {months}, when humpbacks also start passing close to the island's shore.
The cool, dry {months} are best for hiking, and humpback whales pass close to shore from July.
